items.label: f02-stage-tracking
items.front: Which three things does every pipeline stage track per job, and what makes a job eligible for a stage?
items.back: Attempts (<stage>Attempts), error (<stage>Error) and a success marker (timestamp or path). Eligible = success marker missing AND attempts below the configured max - e.g. isNull(detailScrapedAt) and lt(detailAttempts, maxAttempts).

items.label: f01-signal-shutdown
items.front: What happens to the apply stage on SIGINT/SIGTERM (apply/index.ts:129-140, 329-335)?
items.back: A once-handler sets aborted and fires an AbortController, so no new jobs are dequeued; after the workers settle, every job still in progress is marked FAILED (interrupted) and the summary records interrupted.

items.label: f03-one-constant
items.front: A reviewer flags 'string-typed coupling between modules' in the apply stage. What is coupled, and what is the minimal fix?
items.back: fallbackParseIndicator in apply/index.ts regex-matches the English reason produced in parsing.ts; the type system cannot see that contract. Export one constant (or a machine-readable marker on ParsedOutcome) and use it in both places, with a test on the fallback decision.

items.prompt: Someone rewords the parser's "No RESULT line or valid JSON terminal output found" message. What breaks, and what fails in CI?

choices.text: Nothing breaks: fallback keys off the NEEDS_REVIEW status alone
Auto-fallback for parse failures silently dies, and no test fails
TypeScript fails to compile, because the indicator imports the message type
The parsing suite fails, because it snapshots the reason text

choices: Nothing breaks: fallback keys off the NEEDS_REVIEW status alone
Auto-fallback for parse failures silently dies, and no test fails
TypeScript fails to compile, because the indicator imports the message type
The parsing suite fails, because it snapshots the reason text

items.explanation: fallbackParseIndicator regex-matches the English reason string, so the two files agree only on a sentence. The fix is an exported constant or a machine-readable marker on ParsedOutcome used in both files, plus the test that would have caught the regression.

items.prompt: A job has its PDF, applyStatus FAILED, and applyAttempts below the cap. Is it picked up by a normal apply run?

choices.text: Never: FAILED is terminal
No: FAILED is terminal and is never retried
Only when includeFailed is set
Yes, while under the attempts cap

choices: Never: FAILED is terminal
No: FAILED is terminal and is never retried
Only when includeFailed is set
Yes, while under the attempts cap

items.explanation: The or(...) includes eq(applyStatus, 'FAILED') only when includeFailed is true; isNotNull(pdfAt) and lt(applyAttempts, maxAttempts) apply in every case.

items.prompt: An agent prints a valid line "RESULT: FAILED - form error" and, earlier in the output, a bare JSON line {"result":"APPLIED"}. Which outcome wins?

choices.text: FAILED, because the RESULT line is the more explicit terminal contract
APPLIED: the JSON path runs first and returns before RESULT lines are read
NEEDS_REVIEW, because two conflicting terminal markers cancel each other out
FAILED, because the parser always prefers the last line of the output

choices: FAILED, because the RESULT line is the more explicit terminal contract
APPLIED: the JSON path runs first and returns before RESULT lines are read
NEEDS_REVIEW, because two conflicting terminal markers cancel each other out
FAILED, because the parser always prefers the last line of the output

items.explanation: parseAgentOutcome tries parseJsonOutcome and only falls back to parseResultLine when no JSON candidate validates - JSON precedence is one of the three behaviors the parsing suite pins.

items.prompt: With --dry-run, an agent ignores its prompt and really submits the application, then reports APPLIED. What actually protected the employer from a submission?

choices.text: The parser refuses APPLIED outcomes in dry-run mode before the agent exits
The MCP config omits the browser click tool under --dry-run
The Chrome session is opened read-only whenever --dry-run is set
Nothing in code - the DRY_RUN rewrite only keeps the DB honest

choices: The parser refuses APPLIED outcomes in dry-run mode before the agent exits
The MCP config omits the browser click tool under --dry-run
The Chrome session is opened read-only whenever --dry-run is set
Nothing in code - the DRY_RUN rewrite only keeps the DB honest

items.explanation: Dry-run is a prompt-level promise, not a code-level guarantee - a reviewer would want the --dry-run help text ("Run without final submission") to say so.

items.prompt: A scoring call returns JSON whose keys do not match the zod schema. What does the shared LLM helper do next?

choices.text: It retries, telling the model its previous output was invalid for the schema
It returns the parsed object unvalidated and lets the stage handle it
It strips unknown keys and fills any missing ones with schema defaults
It switches to the next LLM provider configured in the pipeline

choices: It retries, telling the model its previous output was invalid for the schema
It returns the parsed object unvalidated and lets the stage handle it
It strips unknown keys and fills any missing ones with schema defaults
It switches to the next LLM provider configured in the pipeline

items.explanation: The loop returns only when schema.parse succeeds; each failure tightens the follow-up prompt so callers receive a typed T or an error.

items.prompt: A job URL is rediscovered by a feed that omits salary, though the stored row has one. What happens to salary and title?

choices.text: Both are overwritten, so the stored salary becomes null
Both are kept, because an existing URL is never updated
A second row is inserted, since the new discovery has different fields
Salary keeps the stored value, while title is overwritten

choices: Both are overwritten, so the stored salary becomes null
Both are kept, because an existing URL is never updated
A second row is inserted, since the new discovery has different fields
Salary keeps the stored value, while title is overwritten

items.explanation: onConflictDoUpdate on jobs.url sets title from excluded unconditionally but coalesces salary, description, location, site, strategy and source.

items.prompt: An agent ends with "RESULT: EXPIRED - posting closed". How does this port treat it?

choices.text: It is stored as a new EXPIRED status in the jobs table
It throws a zod error that aborts the whole apply run
The token is not one of the five statuses, so the output becomes NEEDS_REVIEW
It is folded into FAILED with an EXPIRED prefix, as the Python sibling does

choices: It is stored as a new EXPIRED status in the jobs table
It throws a zod error that aborts the whole apply run
The token is not one of the five statuses, so the output becomes NEEDS_REVIEW
It is folded into FAILED with an EXPIRED prefix, as the Python sibling does

items.explanation: Python maps EXPIRED/LOGIN_ISSUE to FAILED with a prefix; here an unknown token returns null and the loop continues, so without another marker the default NEEDS_REVIEW applies.

items.prompt: Output contains a fenced ```json block with result FAILED, followed later by a bare-line JSON object with result APPLIED. Which candidate is returned?

choices.text: The first candidate found in the raw text, whichever form it takes
The bare-line APPLIED object
Neither; the output is ambiguous
The fenced FAILED block

choices: The first candidate found in the raw text, whichever form it takes
The bare-line APPLIED object
Neither; the output is ambiguous
The fenced FAILED block

items.explanation: Fences are pushed into the candidate list first, bare lines after, and the list is scanned last-to-first - so the bare line wins. Collection order is the implementation's only guard; exercise E2 asks for the test that documents it.

items.prompt: Claude exits 0 but its output has no RESULT line and no JSON. Why does auto mode deliberately NOT fall back to Codex?

choices.text: Because an exit code of 0 is mapped to APPLIED regardless of the output
Exit 0 means the agent believes it finished, so a rerun risks a duplicate application
Because Codex cannot attach to the Chrome session that Claude already used
It does fall back: unparseable output always hands the job to Codex

choices: Because an exit code of 0 is mapped to APPLIED regardless of the output
Exit 0 means the agent believes it finished, so a rerun risks a duplicate application
Because Codex cannot attach to the Chrome session that Claude already used
It does fall back: unparseable output always hands the job to Codex

items.explanation: The condition is a conjunction - exitCode !== 0 && fallbackParseIndicator(...) - which the guide calls the subtlest line in the stage.

items.prompt: An agent's final line is exactly "RESULT: APPLIED" with no dash and no reason. What does parseAgentOutcome return?

choices.text: NEEDS_REVIEW, because the regex requires "- <reason>"
APPLIED with submitted false, because no reason was given
FAILED, because an incomplete marker is treated as an error
APPLIED, with the reason "No reason provided" filled in

choices: NEEDS_REVIEW, because the regex requires "- <reason>"
APPLIED with submitted false, because no reason was given
FAILED, because an incomplete marker is treated as an error
APPLIED, with the reason "No reason provided" filled in

items.explanation: /^result\s*:\s*([a-z_]+)\s*-\s*(.+)$/i makes the dash mandatory. The Python sibling accepts a bare status token, so a shared prompt would silently degrade here.

items.prompt: An agent hallucinates "RESULT: APPLIED - ok" without actually submitting. What does the database record?

choices.text: NEEDS_REVIEW, because "ok" is too short to count as a reason
submitted false, because the RESULT line carries no submitted flag
submitted true, because it defaults to status === APPLIED
APPLIED, pending a secondary check that confirms the submission

choices: NEEDS_REVIEW, because "ok" is too short to count as a reason
submitted false, because the RESULT line carries no submitted flag
submitted true, because it defaults to status === APPLIED
APPLIED, pending a secondary check that confirms the submission

items.explanation: Both parse paths default submitted to status === 'APPLIED'; the Python lineage stores a verification_confidence, this schema does not.

items.prompt: Under --agent auto, Claude exits non-zero but printed a valid "RESULT: CAPTCHA - blocked" line. Does Codex run?

choices.text: Yes: any non-zero exit code triggers the Codex fallback
Yes: CAPTCHA is retryable, so the second backend gets a chance
Only under --dry-run, where a second attempt is harmless
No: a parsed CAPTCHA is a terminal outcome

choices: Yes: any non-zero exit code triggers the Codex fallback
Yes: CAPTCHA is retryable, so the second backend gets a chance
Only under --dry-run, where a second attempt is harmless
No: a parsed CAPTCHA is a terminal outcome

items.explanation: Fallback needs a thrown runner, or a non-zero exit AND the specific no-marker NEEDS_REVIEW. FAILED, CAPTCHA and a genuine NEEDS_REVIEW never trigger Codex, so one job never gets two submission attempts.
